canonical_topic: How gas is physically injected into and held in storage
definition: Storage facilities are underground volumes connected to a pipeline; gas is pulled into them by applying suction (similar to a vacuum) strong enough to overcome the facility's internal pressure.
core_idea: As long as suction on the pipeline connection exceeds the pressure already inside the storage cavity, gas flows into storage rather than back out; once the suction stops, the connection has to be closed off to keep gas from flowing back into the pipeline.
key_points: Storage pressure is normally higher than pipeline pressure unless the facility is nearly empty.
Gas must be compressed to enter the storage facility.
The pipeline-to-storage connection is closed once suction/injection stops.
relationships: Precedes the base gas/working gas withdrawal dynamics.
